articleTitle: Upper Bound on the BEP of IRS-Aided Downlink NOMA System with SIC Errors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Next-generation communication envisaged high reliability while serving multiple users to cater to service quality requirements and massive connectivity. This paper investigates the average bit error rate (BER) performance of the intelligent reconfigurable surface (IRS)-assisted downlink two-user non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems in the presence of imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC) errors. In the proposed IRS-aided NOMA system, the base station broadcasts the information to several users via passive reflectors to exploit the inherent benefits of green communication. The performance of such a system is analyzed in terms of the upper bound and asymptotic expression of average BER to obtain a better insight into the system. In the presence of SIC errors, the system outperforms the conventional NOMA system, and analytical results corroborated with the Monte Carlo simulations. Moreover, the efficacy of the power allocation coefficient on the system performance is investigated.

articleTitle: Message Replication for Improving Reliability of LR-FHSS Direct-to-Satellite IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Long-range frequency-hopping spread spectrum (LR-FHSS) promises to enhance network capacity by integrating frequency hopping into existing Long Range Wide Area Networks (LoRaWANs). Due to its simplicity and scalability, LR-FHSS has generated significant interest as a potential candidate for direct-to-satellite IoT (D2S-IoT) applications. This paper explores methods to improve the reliability of data transfer on the uplink (i.e., from terrestrial IoT nodes to satellite) of LR-FHSS D2S-IoT networks. Because D2S-IoT networks are expected to support large numbers of potentially uncoordinated IoT devices per satellite, acknowledgment-cum-retransmission-aided reliability mechanisms are not suitable due to their lack of scalability. We therefore leverage message-replication, wherein every application-layer message is transmitted multiple times to improve the probability of reception without the use of receiver acknowledgments. We propose two message-replication schemes. One scheme is based on conventional replication, where multiple replicas of a message are transmitted, each as a separate link-layer frame. In the other scheme, multiple copies of a message is included in the payload of a single link-layer frame. We show that both techniques improve LR-FHSS reliability. Which method is more suitable depends on the network’s traffic characteristics. We provide guidelines to choose the optimal method.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Power of Ensemble Algorithms for Diabetes Prediction: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Effective diagnosis of diabetes is crucial for managing the disease and preventing complications. This study explores the use of machine learning for diabetes prediction, focusing on the impact of data preprocessing on model performance. Using four classifiers, namely logistic regression, naive Bayes, random forest, and gradient boosting, diabetes cases are diagnosed after extensive data preprocessing, including cleaning and feature engineering. Results show that the ensemble methods, random forest, and gradient boosting achieve high accuracy and robustness in diabetes prediction, especially with preprocessing. These findings underscore the importance of model selection and preprocessing in healthcare machine learning.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Multi-user OFDM-NOMA Based VLC Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In multi-user visible light communication (VLC) systems, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) combined with DC-biased optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM) is a promising method for improving spectral efficiency. This study presents the practical implementation of a two and three-user NOMA-OFDM-based VLC system, utilizing a laser diode (LD) as the transmitter and a avalanche photodiode (APD) as the receiver. In the three-user configuration, users positioned at $0.5 \mathrm{~m}, 1 \mathrm{~m}$, and 1.5 m are simultaneously served, while in the two-user configuration, users are positioned at $1 \mathbf{m}$ and 2 m from the transmitter. For the two-user case, net data rates of 48.18 Mbps and 96.36 Mbps were achieved using binary phase shift keying (BPSK) and quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM-4) respectively. In the three-user case, data rates of 72.27 Mbps and 144.54 Mbps were achieved using BPSK and QAM-4. For both scenarios, the bit error rate (BER) remained below the target threshold of $10^{-3}$. In the three-user configuration with QAM-4 modulation and a power allocation ratio of $\mathbf{0 . 7 2}$ for the far user, 0.18 for the middle user, and $\mathbf{0 . 0 5}$ for the nearest user, the required optical power levels to achieve the target BER are $-31 \mathrm{dBm},-29.5 \mathrm{dBm}$, and -28 dBm, respectively.

articleTitle: BARET: Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence Enabled Renewable Energy Trading Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Renewable Energy (RE) plays an important role in minimizing the exploitation of natural resources. Also, it helps to reduce the emission of harmful gases in our surroundings. The Blockchain-based Renewable Energy Trading (RET) platform is a futuristic, sustainable solution that allows us to trade RE with less involvement of intermediaries. However, an increase in transaction volume on these platforms leads to delays in transaction confirmation time. Thus, the interest of producers and consumers loses pace. Therefore, we need an alternative solution that can handle the transaction burden without being affected by the increase in producers and consumers participating in the Blockchain-enabled RET platform. In this context, this paper proposed a Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence Enabled Transactive Renewable Energy Trading Framework called BARET. The BARET framework uses the Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence (AI) engine. The Blockchain uses smart contracts to provide trust and transparency in the BARET framework. Also, integrating the Priority-based Double Action using the K-Means clustering (PDA-KC) mechanism to prioritize the number of transactions that are used to store on-chain appropriately. The results demonstrate the suitability of the proposed BARET framework in real-time through a use case. Additionally, a case study using smart contracts and PDA-KC-based results is presented to show the working of the proposed framework. Finally, a tablebased comparison indicates the advantages of the BARET framework over state-of-the-art works.

articleTitle: SentinelMet: Enhancing Metaverse Security through Deep Learning Techniques in 6G
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: With the increasing demand for robust security in the rapidly expanding metaverse within 6 G networks, advanced intrusion detection systems (IDS) are becoming essential. This paper introduces a novel hybrid intrusion detection framework that combines Gaussian Mixture Clustering with Random Forest classifiers and KMeans Clustering with Random Forest classifiers. These models are evaluated for their effectiveness in identifying complex intrusion patterns. The hybrid approaches demonstrated high detection rates, with the Gaussian Mixture Clustering ensemble achieving a detection rate of 99.5-99.6%, while the KMeans clustering model achieved a detection rate of $\mathbf{9 8 - 9 9 \%}$. Comparative analysis shows that these models enhance detection performance while maintaining robustness in a dynamic and diverse metaverse landscape.

articleTitle: CLEAR: A Non-Linear Impairment-Aware Resource Allocation Algorithm for MultiBand Elastic Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Optical networks, characterized by high speed, substantial capacity, and dependable communication, constitute the foundation of 6G Internet of Things (IoT) networks. 6G IoT devices and next-generation applications are expected to generate vast amounts of data that require substantial processing capacity as well as data transport resources, which optical networks are uniquely able to satisfy.However, the existing fiber infrastructure may be unable to accommodate the future bandwidth demands due to 6G networks. MultiBand Elastic Optical Networks (MB-EONs) are one of the possible solutions to solve the capacity crunch problem due to the intensive increase in Internet traffic demand. MB-EONs utilize the unused spectrum of the already deployed optical fiber by extending the bands used from conventional C-band to other optical bands such as L band. However, the increase in capacity comes at the cost of degradation of the quality of transmission of the signal due to the Interband Stimulated Raman Scattering effect. In this paper, we propose Comprehensive Link Evaluation and Allocation for Routing (CLEAR), a Routing, Modulation, Band, and Spectrum allocation algorithm that considers different types of weights of links, i.e., capacity, length, ratio of capacity to length, weighted sum of the normalized link length and capacity, and different fragmentation metrics to find the route that has the most availability of resources among different paths. The results show that reduced blocking performance is observed along with better computational speed when we use the average scoring mechanism and capacity as link weight.

articleTitle: Resource Profiling for Virtualized Radio Access Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The mobile networks are rapidly evolving, transitioning from specialized hardware to fully virtualized platforms that run on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware powered by general-purpose processors. Mobile operators are increasingly adopting Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) to take advantage of virtualization benefits, such as ease of deployment, flexibility, and cost savings. A crucial component of this transformation is the implementation of virtualized Radio Access Network (vRAN) solutions, which provide a cost-effective way to deploy the 5G and beyond RAN as a containerized network function (CNF) on COTS hardware. vRAN is more efficient than traditional RAN, as it allows multiple base station workloads to be multiplexed on the same hardware, potentially co-located with other workloads. However, ensuring consistent performance of vRAN workloads in this consolidated environment is challenging due to the high variability and unpredictability arising from contentions for shared system resources such as CPU cores, Last Level Cache (LLC), and Memory Bandwidth. Thus, there is a strong need to understand the vRAN components if they are affected by any system resource. This paper presents an understanding of how the next-generation scalable processors can be used to run the vRAN components and presents a detailed analysis of the controllable knobs such as CPU, LLC, Memory Bandwidth, and energy consumption. The proposed vRAN profiling shows that the observed throughput varies significantly based on the number of pinned CPU cores (e.g., up to $250 \text{Mbits} / \text{sec}$), and also similar performance observed with other system resources - LLC allocation and Memory Bandwidth.

articleTitle: Detection at Multi-Antenna Reader with Correlated RF Source in Ambient Backscatter Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This work considers a multi-antenna reader and a generalized correlated radio-frequency (RF) source signal in the ambient backscatter communication (AmBC) system. An optimal combining detector (OCD) at the multi-antenna reader is presented for the AmBC system, which detects the signal information embedded by the tag onto a generalized correlated RF source signal. The optimal combining detection statistic for the considered system framework maximizes the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) at the reader. Further, the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) plots for the proposed optimal detector demonstrate superior performance over the allied detectors.

articleTitle: A Generalized Federated Learning Approach for Robust Crop Disease Classification Across Diverse Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In the current scenario, one of the major problems faced by developing countries like India is food security, as the world’s largest population lives here. Plant-based foods are the primary source of food, yet their susceptibility to diseases further compromises the requirements for food security. Although early detection of plant diseases might help in resolving the diseases in crops, farmers may not be able to identify them due to a lack of knowledge and facilities. Deep learning presents a potential solution that identifies diseases using crop images. Although deep learning is a promising solution, it may compromise data privacy because it may require image data from multiple farms. In this work, we produce a federated learning-based privacy-preserving crop disease classification solution where each farm classifies its own data using the Vision Transformer model and only shares model weights with the centralized server. We evaluated the experiment and found that the Vision Transformer, as a base model, provides $\mathbf{9 2 . 0 \%}$ accuracy in disease detection, which we further enhanced to $\mathbf{9 7 . 0 \%}$ with 20 clients. We find this solution promising for AI in agriculture, as it preserves farm data privacy and improves the accuracy of disease classification compared to existing work.

articleTitle: Intelligent Secure Authentication of Smart Devices Using Eye Tracking: Design and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Pattern-based, password-based, and PIN-based authentication techniques are typically the most common among smartphone users. However, according to prior studies these authentication techniques are susceptible to keylogger, smear, and shoulder surfing assaults. These attacks take advantage of data from the user’s handwriting or finger movements. Some research studies restrict eye-tracking authentication for smartphone users because of the regularly controlled environmental circumstances. Currently, no smartphone models support eye-tracking-based authentication. This paper introduces a novel eye-tracking user identification technique using a machine-learning model with inception modules and an ensemble structure for smartphones that eliminates the need for unique hardware or calibration procedures. The goal is to have a favorable influence on the development of an eye-tracking-based method for smart device user verification. The eye movement trajectories as the input to build a character for authentication. These are recorded by the front camera of a smartphone and show the user’s eye movement direction. The proposed application would assist users in situations where they can’t touch their screens for various reasons, such as dirty or stained hands. The proposed method reduces the preprocessing steps typically used in conventional methods. A prototype of the security-based application would be constructed to test the model on a smartphone.

articleTitle: Optimizing Tethered HAP Networks Configuration Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: A tethered High altitude platform station (tHAPS) is a network node that operates in the aeronautical layer at an altitude of around 100 to 150 meters, playing a crucial role in providing communication services. It is linked to the ground through a tether. According to ITU recommendations [1], a tHAPS should have a wide coverage area with a radius of approximately 20 km. A network of multiple tHAPS can extend this coverage to serve an entire country. In this article, we discuss the scenario where multiple tHAPS are distributed across an area, each covering a circular region beneath them. We analyze the reliability of such a system and use a modified Genetic Algorithm (GA) to determine the optimal arrangement of tHAPS for a given region.

articleTitle: Path Planning for Self-driving Vehicles using Metaverse in 6G era with AI-enabled Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Self-driving vehicles are the future of technology which is having the potential to reshape mobility by improving the safety, efficiency, and accessibility of transportation system in 6G networks. Critical task like safety is a crucial factor which is included in the planning of motions of the vehicle through an environment where other vehicles and other objects are part of analysis based on feedback control. This paper mainly focuses on decision-making for autonomous driving, specifically on lane change decisions by using deep reinforcement learning (DRL) in metaverse environment. The challenges of the lane change and path planning addresses the importance of considering both longitudinal speed and lateral lane changes in self-driving vehicle scenarios. The study defines the actions for the autonomous agent like either to stay in the current lane otherwise, changing lanes to the left and right. Thus, safety and efficiency are key concerns in the decision-making process based on rewards and penalties defined to encourage safe driving behavior. The paper limits the self-driving vehicle to drive in the three right lanes of the road to ensure safety and adherence to lane regulations. The goal is to drive as fast as possible within the speed limits, avoid collisions, and minimize unnecessary lane changes in self-driving robots environment. This paper implements longitudinal speed control through rule-based methods while focusing on the lane change decision-making process using reinforcement learning algorithms. Finally, the performance evaluation is performed on Matlab and Simulink to compute the path followed by the proposed model.

articleTitle: DoA Estimation of GNSS Jamming Signal using Tripole Vector Antenna and Random Forest Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper presents an effective strategy for the Global Navigation Satellite System receivers (GNSS) to estimate the direction of arrival (DoA) of jamming signals. A tripole vector antenna is used which consists of three orthogonal dipole antennas. This configuration enables DoA estimation for all directions. A Random Forest Regression (RFR) based model is designed for DoA estimation using the signal received from the tripole vector antenna. Using a baseband receiver processing, the training and testing datasets are prepared. The performance accuracy of the proposed methodology is validated and verified using performance metrics such as $R^{2}$ score and Mean Squared Error. The model hyperparameter number of estimators is tuned on the basis of the said performance metrics. The proposed signal model and regression model are able to estimate DoA of a jamming signal coming from a spinning in both azimuth and elevation. The accuracy of the proposed model in terms of RMSE ranges from 0° to 0.122° for varying jamming to signal ratio (J/S).

articleTitle: Secrecy Performance of UAV-Assisted Underlay Cognitive STBC-NOMA Networks Under Non-Identical Nakagami-m Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The spectrum efficiency of wireless communication networks can be enhanced by incorporating non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and cognitive radio techniques, while unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are a rapid and flexible entity for enhancing coverage performance. This paper considers UAV assisted underlay cognitive network (UCN) with space-time block coding aided NOMA (STBC-NOMA) approach. Herein, the UAV acts as a decode and forward relay to extend the coverage area of a secondary network. In particular, the UAV receives the signals from the secondary transmitter and then retransmits the decoded information to the users using the STBC-NOMA approach. We derive the secrecy outage probability (SOP) and ergodic secrecy rate (ESR) expressions for the secondary users in the presence of an eavesdropper in the network under nonidentical Nakagami-m fading channels. Further, we compare the performance of UAV-assisted UCN using the STBC-NOMA scheme against the NOMA and OMA schemes, which proves the superiority of the STBC-NOMA scheme over the NOMA and OMA schemes in terms of ESR and SOP. Moreover, we provide Monte Carlo simulations to verify the analytical findings.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Strategy for Balancing EDFA and WSS Operating Points for Enhancing Signal Quality in a DWDM System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: A novel strategy for improving signal quality in the DWDM based networks is proposed in this article. Signal quality enhancement in an optical network is a non-trivial task which depends on the operating points and characteristics of the key optical devices like in-line amplifier, pre-amplifier and wavelength selective switch. Commercial-grade devices are used for creating an optical network in CDOT optical testbed and evolution of the strategy for signal quality enhancement. The evolved strategy is validated and compared with the similar approaches described in the literature based on the metrics of optical signal quality. It is observed that the proposed strategy reduces the standard deviation of received channel powers by around $\mathbf{6 5 \%}$ (relative to the baseline strategy) while also improving OSNR. The enhancement in signal quality is validated in multiple spectrum load scenarios. It is also experimentally verified that the proposed strategy is resilient to dynamic changes in the network.

articleTitle: RIS-Assisted Hybrid OMA-NOMA Systems with Imperfect Phase Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: For next-generation wireless communication systems, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are key technology enhancements. However, RIS experiences hardware impairments leading to imperfect phase compensation. In NOMA, user pairing and power allocation are critical for enhancing spectral efficiency. In this paper, we investigate the performance of RIS-assisted NOMA systems with imperfect phase compensation at the RIS. We derive bounds on the power allocation factor to ensure that the achievable data rate for each user surpasses that of a orthogonal multiple access (OMA) system. Based on these bounds, we propose various power allocation algorithms. Furthermore, we introduce a user pairing algorithm designed for hybrid OMANOMA systems, which defaults to OMA to reduce complexity if the achievable sum rate (ASR) gain falls below a specified threshold. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of Solar Panel Communication with Various Phase Shift Keying Modulation Schemes for Light Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: High-speed data transmission and energy-efficient networks are crucial for connecting the world through intelligent communication. Light communication offers high-speed data transfer and is cost-effective due to the vast unlicensed spectrum available. However, there are some challenges at the receiver as it requires an external power supply to operate, and the small area leads to limited orientation and causes misalignment issues. By integrating photovoltaic technology with communication systems, solar panels can resolve the challenges posed by conventional photodiodes and can also serve dual purposes, capturing both solar energy and data signals. This paper presents a bidirectional light communication link to receive information over solar panels. Solar panels convert optical signals into their equivalent electrical form, but their 3-dB bandwidth is limited to a few tens of $\mathbf{k H z}$. To address this limitation, we have designed and experimentally validated an analog circuit that enhances the bandwidth of solar panel-based receivers to 3.07 MHz. The performance comparison with and without designed circuitry is shown, and results are compiled in the form of constellation diagrams with different modulation orders and the transition of the received waveform. The successful recovery of 16 PSK modulation with 32 samples/symbol is obtained.

articleTitle: FedSplit-HIDS: A Host-Based Intrusion Detection Framework for Heterogeneous Industrial IoT Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper presents FedSplit-HIDS, a novel framework aimed at host-based intrusion detection within diverse Industrial Internet of Things (IIOT) environments. The proposed system utilizes a two-fold strategy: Apply federated learning (FL) for devices with ample resources, while incorporating split learning (SL) along with edge computing and FL for devices with limited resources. This approach effectively handles the challenge of processing varied data across multiple IIoT platforms. To enhance privacy protection, localized Rényi differential privacy (L-RDP) is applied at the device level, ensuring the security and privacy of local model parameters and gradients. FedSplit-IDS is equipped to identify a wide range of known intrusions, cyber attacks, and malware that are common in IIoT environments. We suggest that this framework outperforms existing intrusion detection systems in IIoT environments in various evaluation metrics, thus strengthening the critical security infrastructure for Industry 5.0 and integrated cyber-physical manufacturing systems.

articleTitle: Probing the Convergence of Vehicular Edge Metaverse and 6G: Blockchain-enabled Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The convergence of vehicular networks and the Meta-verse, referred to as the Vehicular Edge Metaverse is set to revolutionize both transportation and in-car experiences. This paradigm shift envisions vehicles not only as modes of transport but also as immersive gateways to the Metaverse, offering passengers interactive and engaging experiences while on the move. The advent of 6G, with its ultra-fast speeds and minimal latency is crucial in enabling the real-time data synchronization and low-latency communication required for a seamless Vehicular Edge Metaverse experience. Additionally, blockchain technology can play a key role in ensuring secure and transparent data sharing and transactions within this ecosystem, fostering trust and enabling new business models. This paper explores the potential of this convergence, discussing the key enabling technologies such as 6G, edge computing, and blockchain, and their role in addressing the challenges of real-time synchronization, resource management, and security. Furthermore, we discuss the potential applications like augmented reality-enhanced driving assistance and immersive in-car entertainment, highlighting the transformative impact of the Vehicular Edge Metaverse on the future of transportation.

articleTitle: Exploring New Convolutional Neural Network Architectures for Satellite Image Categorization: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: With deep learning, satellite images can accurately identify land cover elements such as annual crops, forests, herbaceous vegetation, pastures, permanent crops, and rivers. Deep learning has become a valuable tool in this regard. In this field, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown great promise, with pre-trained models such as DenseNet121, EfficientNetB0, VGG16, and InceptionV3 showing encouraging outcomes. To outperform earlier CNN models, this research explores the possibilities of new CNN designs for satellite image categorization. We suggest a comparative study where these more recent architectures are refined using a dataset of satellite images. The results are shown together with a description of how well the above-mentioned CNN models work for this task. The performance is assessed based on accuracy and a discussion of the model’s suitability for this task is included with the result.

articleTitle: The Internet of Trust: Securing and Transparent Supply Chains with Blockchain and IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In an era where digital commerce continues to burgeon, the conventional supply chain confronts challenges of inefficiency, fraud, and a dearth of transparency. Blockchain, renowned for its decentralized and immutable ledger, emerges as a compelling solution to transform the e-commerce supply chain landscape. In conventional supply chain practices marked by centralized databases and manual record-keeping, inefficiencies and a dearth of transparency are widespread. Challenges stemming from cumbersome paperwork, delayed information flow, and vulnerability to errors hindered effective coordination, traceability, and overall operational efficiency. Blockchain and IoT can elevate e-commerce supply chains by ensuring transparent, secure, and automated data-sharing, fostering efficiency and trust throughout the entire process. We have presented an Ethereum-based blockchain and Internet of Things e-commerce platform in this paper. We describe in detail how to put in place a system that stores a product’s journey’s details on an immutable distributed ledger. This allows for secure tracing of a product’s origin. The prototype of the system is deployed and tested on Hardhat testing framework. Traditional databases and cloud storages have been replaced by blockchain and IPFS. IPFS is used as the decentralized and distributed storage layer, facilitating the secure and efficient storage of credentials. Furthermore, the results of our experiments and security and scalability analyses demonstrate the viability of our suggested model.

articleTitle: AirTFT: A Novel Transformer-Based Approach for Air Quality Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Weather planning is vital in public health and environmental conservation thus a necessity for probable accurate air quality forecasting. Benchmarks like ARIMA and SVR derived through statistical methods and machine learning approaches do not work well with non-linear patterns and long term dependencies. Long Short-Term Memory and Gated Recurrent Unit learning algorithms produce higher accuracy than the traditional versions but are not well suited for multiple steps of prediction. This paper presents AirTFT (Air Temporal Fusion Transformer), a new model derived from the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) to overcome these challenges. The used attention mechanism in AirTFT is the dynamic attention which learns to attend to the necessary time steps only for both short and long term dependencies. We benchmark AirTFT on an actual dataset involving hourly air quality recordings, and compare that against ARIMA, SVR, RF, LSTM, GRU, and CNN-LSTM based on MAE, RMSE, and MAPE measures. AirTFT performs better than all models with RMSE and MAPE reduction rates of 35% and 40% compared to LSTM respectively. Furthermore, the results reveal that AirTFT has 50% less MAPE compared to MAPE of ARIMA model and, therefore, AirTFT is superior to all in multi-horizon air quality forecasting. More precisely, AirTFT provides higher accuracy and achieves the goal of predicting temporal related factors, and therefore, can be considered as an efficient instrument to control and improve air quality in real time.

articleTitle: Dynamic Fourier Federated Learning for Fully Connected Distributed Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: As the demand for seamless connectivity across distributed networks increases, traditional federated learning (FL) models struggle to maintain accuracy and efficiency in dynamic environment. Conventional approaches, such as Random Fourier Features-based Kernel Least Mean Squares (RFF-KLMS), often fail to adapt to changing data distributions, leading to performance degradation. To address this issue, the Dynamic Fourier Federated Learning (DFFL) algorithm is introduced, incorporating adaptive Fourier features that iteratively evolve to better align with current data patterns. Simulation results demonstrate that the DFFL algorithm significantly enhances the convergence rate of FL models, ensuring reliable and seamless connectivity in real-world applications where data characteristics are continuously changing.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Battery Depletion Attack in 5G-based UAV Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: 5G introduces various innovations and opportunities across network infrastructures. In 5G, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) can function as relays, and flying base stations to enhance communication availability and meet user demands across a wide range of applications. However, these advancements also bring security threats and malicious activities aimed at disrupting the communication system. One such threat is the Depletion of Battery (DoB) attack. Battery life is a critical component for UAVs, and attackers may attempt to deplete it in various ways, either through physical contact or remotely. Remote attacks can occur via GPS data channels or control channels, with the latter being particularly dangerous. In this work, we focus on an attack using Packet Forwarding Control Protocol (PFCP) messages. These messages are of high priority, requiring immediate attention from the UAV, which attackers exploit to drain the battery by sending numerous unauthorized PFCP messages. To address this attack, we have implemented the CUMSUM method for detection, taking into account the attack vector as a combination of energy consumption, battery depletion, and time. To further enhance our detection approach, we have developed a dynamic threshold strategy to minimize the false positive rate, making our solution more robust and reliable.

articleTitle: A Novel Reliable Routing protocol for MANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In MANETs, nodes connect each other to share information. These nodes move from one place to other and co-operate with each other. Apart from the security, reliability is also one of the main concern in MANETs. Since, most of the devices in the MANET are mobile, mobility degrades the performance of routing protocol. We have proposed a Routing protocol for MANETs which takes mobility as a parameter and establishes a relative reliable path to the destination. our proposed routing protocol increased the throughput and packet Delivery ratio in mobility environment.

articleTitle: Enhancing Mobile Network Security through O-RAN: Architectural Solutions for Physical Layer Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architecture offers unprecedented flexibility, innovation, and security enhancements. This paper explores O-RAN’s application in three critical domains: Localization, Jamming Detection, and Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). By leveraging O-RAN’s open and programmable interfaces, precise localization is enabled for emergency services and asset tracking, while jamming assaults are effectively mitigated to ensure reliable communication. O-RAN’s integration with IDS also strengthens network security through real-time monitoring and sophisticated attack response mechanisms by integrating localization and Jamming Detection. O-RAN adapts to evolving security challenges, improving network performance, resilience, and user satisfaction. At the same time, we are focusing on a set of strategies to develop a solution for physical layer attack detection.

articleTitle: Computing in Transit to Identify Rare Events in Streaming Scientific Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Programmable networks, aside from carrying out their core network functions, can look deep into the data stream and perform application layer processing. But, expect for a few demonstrations, this capability remains largely under explored and under utilized. Currently, scientific computing leverages networks only for communication and not for computation. We propose Computing in Transit to unleash the potential of network computing for scientific workflows. Specifically, we investigate computing in transit in the context of light source experiments. Researchers using light sources are interested in rare events and we intend to leverage computing in transit to solve this problem. As the compute and memory resources available within the network are scarce, we must use these resources prudently without sacrificing on performance metrics. Computing within the network can support significantly higher throughput at low latency but it may be less accurate as there are limitations to how deep a network can inspect the payload. We propose a neutralized checksum that takes in TCP checksum as an input to avoid processing the entire payload. We evaluate this approach to identify rare events by introducing random perturbations to reference frames. We measure the effectiveness of neutralized checksum to identify changes. We see that neutralized checksum identifies all changes and is a very promising approach to rare event detection.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in WBANs using Semi-Supervised Double Deep Q-Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) seamlessly interconnects wearable devices on the human body, enabling the monitoring of diverse physiological parameters for better health outcomes. Ensuring the accuracy and security of data transmission is essential to avert the occurrence of false alarms and maintain the overall reliability of WBANs. The substantial volume of data exchanged within WBANs heightens the vulnerability to data attacks or the transmission of noisy or erroneous data, necessitating real-time handling capabilities. Moreover, the availability of labeled datasets is limited. Consequently, this research proposes a semi-supervised Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) model capable of real-time detection of false alarms within the data. This model incorporates a DDQN featuring a Deep Neural Network architecture that includes an LSTM layer and several Dense layers to capture the intricate spatiotemporal relationships within the dataset and classify the data received into normal or faulty categorical data. The semi-supervised DDQN model leverages a K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) classifier to assign labels to the unlabeled data extracted from the MIMIC-1 dataset. Subsequently, this labeled data is forwarded to the DDQN model for prediction. To validate the efficacy of the semi-supervised DDQN model, we have performed extensive testing, resulting in an accuracy of 98.9%, a recall of 96.48%, a precision of 92.25%, an F1 score of 94.32%, and a false-positive rate of 0.85%.

articleTitle: AURA: Adaptive Unified Real-Time Analytics for IoT Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In high-volume, high-velocity contexts, threat identification requires effective real-time data stream analysis. This study offers a novel architecture—real-time processing of high-speed data streams—that is critical for effective threat identification in dynamic contexts. By using a publish-subscribe approach with Apache Kafka, the system is able to manage differences in data volume between many nodes. Experiments on the CICIoV24 and the CICEVSE2024 datasets indicate that the XGBoost model performs better, with high accuracy and robustness against adversarial attacks. Its performance degrades during the HopSkipJump attack, however, defence training can help with it. Moreover, our analysis shows that RandomForest and ExtraTrees perform better in noisy data from the CICIoV24 and XGBoost perform better in noisy data from the CICEVSE24 dataset, emphasizing the importance of selecting algorithms based on performance indicators. The architecture utilizes PyFlink’s distributed computation framework to improve computational efficiency for real-time processing and solves idea drift to ensure flexibility in changing data attributes.

articleTitle: Mitigating Cross-Site Request Forgery Vulnerabilities: An Examination of Prevention Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) remains a pervasive vulnerability in web applications, appearing regularly in the OWASP Top 10 lists, posing significant threats to user data and system integrity despite the existence of numerous rectification methodologies. This study undertakes a thorough, comprehensive analysis of the present environment of CSRF prevention systems, investigating their operational mechanisms, effectiveness, and associated limitations. Hence, this paper explores the role of CSRF tokens in the prevention of cyberattacks, including the detection of token absence and the implementation of token-based countermeasures to mitigate CSRF risks. The system model utilizing simple JavaScript and Flask Applications that aim to utilize the token-based countermeasure to identify the existence of tokens and generate and append them to requests, which ensures security of user data and system integrity.

articleTitle: Dynamic Resource Assignment Technique for 6G Wireless Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In the current article, a dynamic resource assignment (DRA) technique is proposed for assigning key resources dynamically for 6G wireless system. DRA implements an opportunistic spectrum sharing (SS) method which uses cooperative SS to enable secondary users (SUs) in detecting any vacant spectrum slots not being currently utilized by primary users (PUs). The aim of DRA is to maximize overall throughput of SUs simultaneously ensuring desired quality of service for PUs. To achieve the aim, DRA adjusts time for spectrum sensing in accordance with detection probabilities of target and false alarms. The results reveal that DRA is effective in obtaining desired solutions, and it is mandatory to adjust time for sensing.

articleTitle: Traffic Control Analysis in High Altitude Platforms using a Semi-Markov Process Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This study uses a cooperative communication approach to propose a traffic model for relay nodes in space-airground networks. The proposed model is employed in threelayer networks: low earth satellite (LEO), high altitude platform (HAP), and user devices on the ground. This type of aerial communication network is adopted in most Internet of Things (IoT) networks. The analysis has been carried out by constructing traffic models. The traffic model has been analyzed by applying the semi-Markov process due to the non-exponential behaviour of some of the transitions of states. The network’s practical lifetime, the average delay of source/relay packets, and throughput are investigated through the novel traffic model. Finally, through numerical illustrations, the impact of the performance measures is shown by conducting a sensitivity analysis.

Author Keywords: cooperative communication, high altitude platform, low earth orbit, semi-Markov process, and traffic model

articleTitle: Hierarchical BiLSTM-LSTM Network for Short-Term Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Accurate residential load forecasting is essential for demand response in the evolving intelligent and interactive power system framework. Short-term load forecasting for individual electric customers has become increasingly critical for future grid planning and operations. However, predicting the electric load of a single consumer presents significant challenges due to the highly stochastic nature of individual usage patterns. This study proposes an enhancement to the widely adopted long shortterm memory (LSTM) networks by incorporating hierarchical Bi-directional LSTM (BiLSTM) and LSTM layers, and comprehensive feature engineering to improve model performance in capturing individual consumer behavior. We optimize feature selection using the chi-squared test, and the proposed approach, compared to its counterparts, demonstrates improvements in prediction accuracy with a reduction of $8.31 \%$ in mean absolute percentage error compared to the baseline gated recurrent unit method. These results underscore the potential of integrating advanced feature engineering techniques with deep learning methods for more precise individual residential load forecasting.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Active RIS-assisted Full-Duplex-Two-Way NOMA System under Finite Blocklength with Hardware Impairments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The active reconfigurable intelligent surface’s (ARIS) potential of avoiding multiplicative fading loss by utilizing integrated reflection-type amplifiers has drawn considerable interest. This paper investigates the performance of ARIS-assisted full-duplex two-way (FDTW) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) (ARIS-FDTW-NOMA) systems under finite blocklength (FBL) transmission regimes by using cascaded Nakagamim fading channels under hardware impairments (HIs). In this system, two users exchange their information simultaneously through NOMA with the help of ARIS. To assess the system performance, we derived the novel analytical expression of average block error rate (ABLER) and system throughput with the help of the Gauss Laguerre quadrature (GLQ) and Gauss Chebyshev quadrature (GCQ) method. Asymptotic analysis is also done at higher transmit power regimes to obtain useful insights. We have also compared the performance of the ARISFDTW- NOMA system with passive-RIS-FDTW-NOMA (PRISFDTW- NOMA) and ARIS-FDTW-orthogonal multiple access (ARIS-FDTW-OMA). Monte Carlo simulations are performed to verify the accuracy of the analytical expressions. Numerical results reveal that our proposed ARIS-FDTW-NOMA system outperforms PRIS-FDTW-NOMA and ARIS-FDTW-OMA scenarios in terms of ABLER and system throughput.

articleTitle: FogIoT: Fog Computing based Security Frameworks for Software-defined IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Software-defined Networking (SDN) has been implemented in Internet of things (IoT) networks to attain centralized control and improve network management. However, the SDN centralized approach can be compromised by malicious sensor nodes engaging in activities like message dropping or flooding, which can negatively impact the network’s functionality. The security measures in the IoT networks are often based on an idealized trusted environment, which is not practical due to resource constraints and high computational requirements. In this paper, we proposed a lightweight cryptographic approach for detecting potential security threats in wireless fog-enabled SDN-IoT network named as FogIoT. To improve detection of attacks on control plane traffic, the proposed approach examines the credibility of network nodes using reliability metrics and a reliability index. We also propose an acknowledgment-based mechanism to capture reliability and used a weighted averaging approach to determine the confidence index for nodes to ensure credibility. We demonstrated a simulation study to analyze the performance of the lightweight cryptography algorithm and results from simulations show that FogIoT is effective in detecting various types of attacks such as sink-hole, denial of service, and reputation-deceptive.

articleTitle: Secrecy Performance Analysis of RIS-assisted System Under Nakagami-m Fading
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a system comprising of a source node, two reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) nodes, a legitimate destination, and an eavesdropper. One of the two RIS sides supports the legitimate destination in enhancing its data detection capability. The second RIS side is malicious and assists the eavesdropper in overhearing legitimate communication. The system is affected under Nakagami- m fading. We analyze the secrecy performance of the system in terms of secrecy outage probability (SOP), probability of strictly positive secrecy capacity (PSPSC), secrecy ergodic capacity (SEC), and intercept probability (IP). We opt for generalized- K (KG) and mixture gamma (MG)-based approximation methods to provide an accurate analysis for an arbitrary number of RIS-reflecting elements and fading parameters. We also derive the asymptotic SOP expression to provide a simplified analysis at high signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs). The analytical results are validated with the simulated results. We also highlight some observations drawn based on the analysis.

articleTitle: An Energy Efficient UAV Path Planning for Data Collection in Multi-Node IoT System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become indispensable instruments in various applications, including surveillance, environmental monitoring, and data collection in Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications. The effectiveness and efficiency of UAV missions are inextricably linked to the path-planning strategies employed. With the modern approach to minimization, the requirement to minimize UAV energy consumption and boost battery time available is growing rapidly. With this objective, this paper presents Energy Constrained-Adaptive Path Construction (EC-APC), as an improved optimization technique for UAV path planning keeping in consideration the battery limits of the UAV. The proposed algorithm, named MNES, uses EC-APC to generate several paths for the UAV to satisfy its energy constraints. Simulation results and complexity analyses corroborate the time complexity advantage and energy-efficient path planning of the proposals.

articleTitle: Impact of noise in distance-based short text clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Efficient text clustering is essential for applications like recommendation systems, trend analysis, and user profiling, particularly when dealing with data from online repositories such as social media platforms. However, the effectiveness of clustering methods is significantly impacted by the inherent challenges of such data, including sparsity, short text length, and unstructured nature. One of the most critical challenges is the prevalence of noise in the data, manifested through slang, emojis, misspellings, abbreviations, and grammatical errors, which can severely degrade clustering performance. This research examines the robustness of distance-based clustering algorithms against noisy data by systematically introducing noise directly into the text. We introduce two types of noise–attribute noise and class noise for effective noise injection. We analyze the ability of different distance measures to differentiate meaningful content from irrelevant information under these noise-induced conditions. Through a series of experiments, we evaluate the degradation in clustering accuracy of various distance measures in the presence of noise, providing valuable insights into their noise tolerance and practical utility in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Increasing Information-Carrying Capacity by Exploiting Diverse Traffic Characteristics in Multi-Band Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Efficient network management in optical backbone networks is crucial for handling continuous traffic growth. In this work, we address the challenges of managing dynamic traffic in C- and C+L-band optical backbone networks while exploring application flexibility, namely the compressibility and delayability metrics. We propose a strategy, named Delay-Aware and Compression-Aware (DACA) provisioning algorithm, which reduces blocking probability, thereby increasing information-carrying capacity of the network compared to baseline strategies.

articleTitle: Facility Location in 6G-aware Vehicular Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper tackles the facility location problem in 6G -enabled Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) systems, focusing on the optimal placement of Roadside Units (RSUs) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The goal is to minimize Quality of Service (QoS) degradation by addressing challenges like dynamic vehicle mobility, traffic variations, and real-time task offloading. A mathematical optimization model is proposed, considering latency, energy consumption, packet loss, and handover costs. To solve this complex problem, heuristic algorithms such as Hill Climbing, Tabu Search, Simulated Annealing, and A* search are introduced. Extensive simulations evaluate their performance on energy efficiency and cumulative latency across various traffic and network conditions. The results reveal the strengths of each algorithm, offering valuable insights for their application in VEC scenarios. These findings contribute to scalable, energy-efficient solutions for 6G-aware VEC networks, particularly in dynamic vehicular environments, advancing research in edge computing and network optimization.

articleTitle: A Low Complexity Segmented Parity SC Flip Decoding Algorithm for Polar Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The Successive Cancellation decoder cannot provide satisfactory error correcting performance for finite length polar codes. The error performance can be improved by using Successive Cancellation Flip decoders at the expense of higher complexity. In line with this, a novel decoding approach has been developed in this paper, where distributed parity bits are used to divide the codeword into multiple segments having equal probability of error occurrence, allowing early termination. The proposed Segmented Parity Successive Cancellation Flip (SP-SC Flip) Decoder achieves lower normalized complexity and average decoding latency compared to some related existing decoders, without degrading the error correcting performance. Further improvement in decoder performance is observed when code words are divided into a greater number of segments.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of Adding Links on Network Availability and Max-flow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Network Availability (NA) is the probability that all the network flows can be routed at a given time instant. Max-flow of a source-destination pair is the maximum traffic volume that can be routed between them. High $N A$ and max-flow are necessary for future Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC). This work identifies the best links to add to the network to maximize $N A$ and max-flow cost-efficiently and discusses the trade-off between $N A$, max-flow, and cost.

articleTitle: Exponential Hyperbolic Cosine Robust Adaptive Diffusion Strategy for Distributed Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper presents a robust adaptive diffusion algorithm based on exponential hyperbolic cosine cost function to enhance the distributed estimation performance. Mathematical analysis shows the convergence criteria of the algorithm. Performance analysis of the proposed algorithm is carried out in terms of convergence speed and steady-state expected mean square error (EMSE), and also the performance is compared with other diffusion algorithms called d-LMS and d-NMVC. The robustness of the proposed algorithm is shown by simulation results for Gaussian noisy environment as well as for different non-Gaussian noisy environments.

Author Keywords: Diffusion Exponential Hyperbolic Cosine Adaptive Filter (d-EHCAF)

articleTitle: KNOXRT: Knowledge-Networked Optimization for eXploratory Real-time Training
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Effective threat detection and classification are essential in real-time data stream processing. In this paper, KNOXRT, an architecture that combines traditional tree-based models, such as Random Forest, XGBoost, and CART, with deep learning models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long ShortTerm Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), is presented. Real-time data is ingested using Apache Kafka, and feature extraction is performed in parallel through CNN, CNN+LSTM, and CNN+GRU models. The resulting features are merged and passed through multiple classifiers, achieving high classification accuracy. The best-performing model, CART, achieved perfect training accuracy (1.00) and strong production testing accuracy (0.9927), precision (0.9927), recall (0.9927), and F1-score (0.9927). Class imbalances are addressed using GSmote for balanced training data, and real-time predictions are supported by containerized microservices. Continuous performance monitoring and online retraining ensure the system adapts to dynamic environments without interruption.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration for Co-existance of DPS-QKD Channel over C+L Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Considering the fact that quantum key distribution(QKD) require dark fiber, but laying new fiber or using an dedicated fiber for QKD may not be possible in all instance, a pratical situations consider where multiplexing involving the quantum channel required for DPS QKD and the classical situation present in the same fiber is done. Such a practical situation is realised experimentally to reveal that there exists trade off between classical data rate and secure key rate obtained by the QKD protocol. The existence of this trade-off indicates that in the above situation where quantum and classical channel coexists in a fiber or telecom operator would require to optimize classical channel power, channel separation and our results indicate that an operator will need to optimize in terms of classical channel power, channel separation, and number of channels to achieve a substantial key rate and data rate while operating over filled C and $\text{C}+\text{L}$ Band scenarios.

articleTitle: Performance Characterization of an IRS-assisted OFDM System with HPA Memory Effects and IRS Phase Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In the realm of forthcoming wireless communication systems, various technologies have emerged, with intelligent reflective surfaces (IRSs) standing out as a promising contender for enhancing spectral and energy efficiency. The effectiveness of such systems is significantly impaired by the nonlinear characteristics inherent in their components. This work examines the collective impact of nonlinearity stemming from memory effects in high power amplifiers (HPAs) and phase noise from the IRS on an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system. Specifically, the performance is evaluated by deriving mathematical expressions for determining the outage probability (OP), spectral efficiency (SE), and energy efficiency (EE) in an OFDM communication system augmented by an IRS, while considering the effects of non-ideal HPA and phase noise in the IRS. We validate our analytical results through comparison with simulations, confirming the accuracy of our approach. Our findings highlight the significant impact of HPA nonlinearity and IRS phase noise on the performance of the above communication system.

articleTitle: TMD-Tradeoff and Slide Attack Analysis on the Novel ZUC-PRN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The rapid evolution of wireless communication technologies is epitomized by the advent of 5G-Advanced and the forthcoming 6G era. While 5G-Advanced enhances existing capabilities, 6G aims to seamlessly integrate AI-driven intelligence and sophisticated cryptographic techniques, significantly bolstering security. This paper explores the ZUC-PRN model [1], a neural network-based cipher inspired by the ZUC algorithm, proposed for enhancing wireless security in 5G and 6G networks. While ZUC-PRN shows potential for replacing traditional FSM-based ciphers, its resilience against various attacks remains unverified. We analyze its vulnerabilities to Slide and Time-Memory-Data Tradeoff (TMDT) attacks and assess its computational complexity, comparing it with the standard ZUC stream cipher. This study provides critical insights into the security and efficiency of the ZUC-PRN model, contributing to the development of more robust encryption methods for next-generation communication systems.

articleTitle: Advancements in M-Healthcare for the Detection and Management of Brain Metastases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Brain metastases (BM) are secondary brain tumors originating from cancer cells that have spread from primary tumors in other parts of the body, and they are the most common type of brain tumor in adults. Primary cancers that frequently metastasize to the brain include lung, breast, melanoma, and renal cell carcinoma. These metastases significantly impact patient morbidity and mortality, with treatment strategies involving surgical resection, radiation therapy, systemic therapies, and stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS). The localization and segmentation of brain metastases tackle numerous pivotal challenges in the clinical management of cancer patients. Deep learning models for detection are essential for improving treatment efficacy and patient outcomes by enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of identifying metastatic lesions. Additionally, integrating mobile healthcare (m-healthcare) solutions enables continuous patient monitoring, real-time data collection, and remote consultations. This integration supports personalized care, timely treatment adjustments, and improved patient adherence, ultimately enhancing the quality of care and life for patients with brain metastases. The aim of this project is to develop an efficient patient-centered approach using deep learning and m-healthcare technologies to improve the detection, monitoring, and treatment of brain metastases, thereby optimizing patient outcomes and quality of life.

articleTitle: Simultaneously Transmitting And Reflecting (STAR) IRS-Aided OTFS System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: We develop a novel and comprehensive model for a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting (STAR) intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) system. We propose two novel algorithms, namely, equal split STAR IRS phase programming and two step amplitude and phase programming, to reconfigure both the transmission and reflection coefficient of the passive elements in an STAR IRS-aided OTFS system and also analyze their computational complexities. We show that the second algorithm performs noticeably better than the first at marginally higher complexity. We also elucidate that an STAR IRS outperforms a conventional IRS in an OTFS system as the number of passive elements increases. Our work also suggests that 3-bit discrete phase shifts at the STAR IRS can achieve the same BER performance as an STAR IRS with infinite phase precision.

articleTitle: Secure and privacy focused electronic health record management framework using blockchain and IPFS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The demand for efficient health record management systems in India has become increasingly apparent in recent years due to the country’s vast and diverse healthcare landscape. In response to this need, this study proposes the development of a comprehensive full-stack health record management system tailored specifically for the Indian healthcare context. The system aims to streamline the collection, storage, and retrieval of patient health records, ensuring accessibility, accuracy, and security throughout the healthcare ecosystem. This proposed system have front-end as well as back-end components, providing users with a seamless and intuitive interface for interacting with patient data. Leveraging modern technologies, the proposed framework front-end interface will Furthermore, the development of this full-stack health record management system will involve extensive collaboration with healthcare stakeholders across India, including hospitals, clinics, government agencies, and regulatory bodies. By fostering partnerships and incorporating feedback from end-users, this system goal is to address the unique challenges and requirements of the Indian healthcare ecosystem, ultimately contributing to improved patient care, enhanced data interoperability, and more efficient healthcare delivery nationwide.

articleTitle: Adaptive Trajectory Planning in Autonomous Vehicles: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Approach with Soft Actor-Critic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This study introduces a methodology enabling automated vehicles to perform lane changes effectively within complex road systems. It emphasizes a hierarchical driver behavior framework that integrates decision-making with trajectory planning to enhance safety. The approach utilizes reinforcement learning (RL) agents for automated vehicles and the MOBIL model for human-operated vehicles, aiming to optimize the lane change process. The paper introduces the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), an off-policy actor-critic algorithm, to improve training stability and effectiveness in real-world robotics applications. Additionally, it offers a comprehensive review of existing planning and control algorithms for self-driving vehicles, offering a comprehensive survey of techniques and their strengths and limitations to aid in informed design choices.

articleTitle: Fingerprint-Based Multifactor Authentication For Bank Transaction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Robberies of ATMs have been on the rise in the last few years and are becoming a major concern for Banks and their customers. Currently, we operate ATMs using a PIN that can become a victim of theft, guessed, and can be hacked while the transaction is going on. This raises a question on the security of ATM transactions and requires new techniques and schemes that can offer a second level of protection. Considering these security concerns, we proposed a security check on the existing ATM systems. We authors have created two applications that present the new technique. Our banking application, called Fingerpay, works like traditional banking applications with an added feature where the user can enable the MFA (Multi-factor Authentication) through MPIN verification. In this case, a request for fingerprint authentication is prompted as a notification on the user’s registered mobile number. Upon successful authentication, the transaction is authorized and completed securely. The key contribution of this research lies in the formation of a secure and user-friendly MFA system for ATM transactions. By integrating fingerprint authentication with existing banking applications, users are prompted to verify their identity through a registered fingerprint scan during ATM transactions. This additional layer of authentication increases security by significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized access and fraudulent transactions. In addition, biometric authentication outperforms traditional methods, including increased accuracy, reliability, and resistance to identity theft or impersonation. In the end, this proposal will go a long way in resolving the problem of ATM transactions. Further, this report contains the introduction, design and implementation part of the proposed model.

articleTitle: ResCNNGRU: A Hybrid Deep Learning Based Algorithm for Modulation Classification in NOMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is pivotal in non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems, as it dynamically adjusts modulation schemes to maximize spectral efficiency and minimize inter-user interference. We introduce a novel deep learning (DL) based architecture that integrates a residual convolutional neural network (CNN) with a gated recurrent unit (GRU) to classify the modulation formats of the interference users in NOMA downlink scenarios. This hybrid model harnesses the strengths of both spatial and temporal patterns extracted from the superposed in-phase and quadrature-phase (IQ) signals. Through comprehensive experimentation, we observe that for power ratio 4 and 200 symbol points our model demonstrates an accuracy of more than $99 \%$ at signal-to-noise (SNR) levels of 6 dB and above. This approach not only surpasses existing methods in classification accuracy but also proposes a computationally efficient modulation classifier.

articleTitle: Spectrum Status Aware Dynamic Routing and Spectrum Allocation in Elastic Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The flexible grid multiplexing technique in Elastic Optical Network (EON) offers enhanced spectral efficiency and greater flexibility. However, a significant challenge in these networks is the increased blocking probability due to increased flexibility. To address this, we have introduced a dynamic weight mechanism in which the link weights are determined by the maximum unoccupied contiguous spectrum slices present in them. The link weight is relative which depends on the other link’s spectrum status. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed algorithm reduces blocking probability more effectively than the benchmark algorithms by incorporating spectrum constraint-related status into link weights, leading to improved spectrum utilization.

articleTitle: FGF-CNN: Federated Gradient Fusion For Convolutional Neural Networks – A Collaborative Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Federated learning is a type of technique that makes it possible to train the models using a centralized process, at the same time ensuring that individual privacy is observed. We also propose the Federated Gradient Fusion Convolutional Neural Network (FGF-CNN) to which the gradient fusion technique is applied for the global integration of local architectures in this paper. The FGFCNN is intended for image classification tasks through the use of a CNN inclusive of two dimensional convolution layer, the Max Pooling layer, flattening process as well as a fully connected softmax layer. The proposed model was trained under the SugarCane dataset which harbors several types of sugarcane image classes. The method being proposed uses client side gradient updates that make the results more generalizable than the raw data used which in turn helps with privacy considerations. The results lead to high accuracy and efficiency in federated environments with a lower number of exchanged messages counted as a communication overhead, which makes FGF-CNN applicable to real-world distributed learning setups where the data privacy is a concern.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation over 400 km C+L Band Optical Testbed for Quality of Transmission Estimation Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Multiband transmission (MBT) has appeared as an immediate solution for the network operator to solve the optical fiber capacity crunch problem. However, the quality of the transmission (QoT) in MBT becomes susceptible to nonlinear impairments (NLI) due to the presence of interchannel stimulated Raman scattering (ISRS). This paper considered the scenario of $\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{L}$ band optical transmission, as the additional transmission over L-band becomes the first stepping stone towards the commercialization of MBT. We have experimentally investigated the signal transmission over the $400 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{C}+\mathrm{L}$ band optical link while using different band-specific amplifiers and transceiver modules. Two launch powers per channel, -1.5 dBm and 0 dBm, have been considered for both 200G DP-QPSK and 400G DP16QAM signal transmission. Multiple real and dummy channels have been multiplexed to generate a 100 GHz spaced WDM spectrum with 96 total channels. The positions of the real channels are tuned across the $C+L$ band spectrum, and the optical power profile across different channels is collected for individual scenarios using the optical spectrum analyzer (OSA). In addition, the QoT has been monitored in terms of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), Q-factor, and bit-error-rate (BER). In order to leverage the advantage of machine learning (ML) techniques for next-generation optical network designing, these monitoring data have been used, and random forest (RF)-based regressor models have been utilized for QoT estimation. Reported results indicate that the estimation error lies within 1 dB for SNR and Q-factor regressor models, whereas the BER estimator achieves a maximum estimation error of 0.009 units.

articleTitle: SWIPT-NOMA Enabled Hybrid VLC/RF System for Dynamic Indoor Workspaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Hybrid visible light communication (VLC)/ radio frequency (RF) systems offer a promising solution for indoor wireless communication by leveraging the strengths of both technologies. RF provides robust, long-range communication, while VLC offers high data rates and security, making their combination ideal for diverse applications in indoor environments. Integrating simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) further enhances these hybrid systems by enabling efficient energy harvesting and higher spectrum utilization. In this paper, we consider user mobility in a SWIPT-NOMA enabled hybrid VLC/RF system with predictive handover mechanisms, namely, immediate vertical handover (IVHO) and dwell vertical handover (DVHO). We analyze the transfer delay and the throughput performance between VLC and RF access points to ensure a reliable and seamless connectivity to the mobile users. Through simulations, we demonstrate that the proposed SWIPT-NOMA-based handover strategy significantly outperforms traditional NOMA-based handover methods, offering improved reliability and efficiency in a dynamic indoor scenario.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer
Author Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT)

articleTitle: An Energy Measurement Framework for 5G RAN Using USRP and Real-Time Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Beyond 5G (B5G) networks, expected to support applications requiring ultra-low latency, high data rates, and dense connectivity, may increase energy consumption, especially in the Radio Access Network (RAN), which accounts for about 75% of total mobile network energy usage. We present an architecture for precise measurement of RAN energy consumption by monitoring the gNB radio interface implemented with Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) and OpenAirInteraface (OAI). Real-time measurements from the GW Instek GPM-8213 power meter allowed us to analyze energy consumption patterns during various gNB operation phases. Our results show precise measurement and differentiation of energy usage during user transmission, enabling exact operational cost quantification. This architecture enables energy measurements in other mobile scenarios, paving the way for advanced network management use cases and more energy-efficient B5G operations.

articleTitle: IRS-Assisted Hybrid Spatial Modulation for Full-Duplex MIMO Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
