Moreover, existing domain adaptation (DA) models could not sufficiently reap the domain-shared features well from multiple source, questioning the models’ applicability. Complex structure of these DA models tends to a nominal performance gain due to inefficient resource utilization of the sources. The present paper introduces a domain adaptation deep neural network model, Bootstrap Zero-Shot (BTS-Z) learning model which focuses on capturing the latent spatio-temporal features of the whole city traffic network shared among every source city and maneuver them to predict for the target city traffic network with no prior information. The presented model proves the efficacy of the bootstrap algorithm in the prediction of demands for the unseen target over the computationally expensive MAML models. The experimental results on three real-world city taxi data on the standard benchmark metrics report a minimum of 23.41% improvement over the best performing competitive system.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Accelerated Antenna Selection for an Underlay Spectrum Sharing System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) techniques can help reduce the computational complexity of antenna selection (AS) for an underlay spectrum sharing system, which enables efficient spectrum utilization. We illustrate this by proposing two ML approaches: i) A supervised learning based classification approach with instantaneous channel power gains as input and antenna index as output. It predicts antenna index directly with low complexity; ii) A model-based regression approach with system parameters such as the number of antennas, fixed transmit power, and channel statistics as inputs and a parameter required to implement the conventional AS rule as output. It substitutes the obtained parameter in the conventional $A S$ rule to select the antenna index and exploits the structure of the optimal AS rule. Furthermore, it generalizes to different system parameters and reduces training overhead significantly. We show that both neural network and random forest models trained for the above approaches are near-optimal. We also show that these models work for different channel models including 3GPP adapted tap delay line models while requiring orders of magnitude lower amount of time.

articleTitle: A Static Analysis Approach to Verify Data Integrity of Web-based Software Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Web-based application plays an important role in our day-to-day activities. Such kinds of applications deal with large volumes of data access and data manipulation continuously. Data security is one of the prime concerns for data access. During any operation on data, it is important to preserve the data integrity to maintain security. In this work, we provide a static analysis approach to verify data integrity to ensure the data security of web-based applications. We used an abstract-based static analysis technique with the help of the powerset domain of interval to analyze the actual behavior of the system.

articleTitle: MMV-Aided Bayesian Learning for Simultaneous Sparse Channel Estimation in Visible Light DCO-OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: A multipath channel impulse response (CIR) estimator is introduced, utilizing the simultaneous sparsity across multiple measurement vectors (MMV) for direct current-biased optical OFDM (DCO-OFDM) visible light communication (VLC) systems. The multipath CIR model incorporates both diffusive and specular reflections in the VLC channel. The system model for the DCO-OFDM is formulated, followed by traditional and compressive sensing (CS)-based channel estimation (CE) methods, such as simultaneous sparse orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) and Bayesian learning (BL). An advanced estimation method using MMV-based Bayesian learning (MBL) is proposed, reducing pilot overhead by leveraging simultaneous sparsity. Benchmarks like the Oracle-minimum mean squared error (O MMSE) estimator and the Bayesian Cramer Rao lower bound (BCRLB) are derived for performance comparison. Simulation results show that the proposed MMV-based MBL method outperforms other techniques in normalized mean-square-error (NMSE), pilot overhead, and bit error-rate (BER), closely match the benchmarks derived.

articleTitle: PUF-based Lightweight Mutual Authentication Scheme for IoT-based Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Smart grids have paved the way for the amalgamation of electricity and the Internet of Things (IoT). IoT enables communication of important data, such as electricity consumption, between the smart meter and the server. At the same time, it makes the system vulnerable to cyber-attacks as the IoT devices are resource-constrained in nature and not equipped with adequate in-built security. Thus, secure and lightweight authentication schemes are of utmost need. Existing literature on lightweight authentication schemes are either computationally heavy specifically during authentication operations or need high communication and storage requirements. This paper mainly focuses on authentication phase as it is executed many times in the lifespan of an IoT device compared to the device registration phase. To address the above issues, this paper proposes a lightweight mutual authentication scheme that can protect the system from various attacks such as man-in-the-middle (MITM) and replay attacks. The proposed scheme uses physically unclonable function (PUF) primitives of IoT devices to alleviate the long-term storage requirement in the devices and further makes the scheme secure by achieving operational asymmetry. Unlike many existing schemes, our proposed scheme performs the device enrolment phase through the insecure channel as in many real-world applications. We have verified the security of the proposed scheme through formal and informal analysis. Further, we have done a test-bed implementation and analysis using off-the-shelf available hardware to represent IoT devices. In all the analysis, it is observed that the proposed scheme is lightweight and secure compared to the state-of-the-art schemes.

articleTitle: Evaluating Energy Efficiency in Two-Way MIMO CRNs: A Joint Approach to Relay Selection and Precoder Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper explores the energy-efficiency (EE) performance of a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) equipped cognitive radio network, where multiple two-way (TW) half-duplex (HD) relays facilitate communication between two secondary transceivers (STs). To achieve full diversity with reduced complexity, we employ relay selection through three distinct schemes. We further optimize the precoders at both transceivers and selected relay node to maximize the EE of the secondary system (SS), while taking into account quality-of-service (QoS), transmit power, and interference constraints. The resulting non-convex optimization problem is addressed using a combination of singular value decomposition (SVD), fractional programming theory, and an alternating optimization algorithm. Numerical results demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed solution in enhancing the EE and the probability of feasibility (PoF) of the SS.

articleTitle: Forecasting and Mitigating Interference in TDD Mobile Communication Networks Using Machine Learning: A Data-Driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods to predict potential cross-link interference occurrences in Time Division Duplex (TDD) networks and identify optimal interference mitigation strategies. By combining network performance data with weather information, our objective is to establish predictive models capable of anticipating interference challenges and suggesting proactive solutions. Utilizing datasets obtained from a prominent Indian telecommunication provider, enriched with meteorological data, we train and evaluate the models. Through the implementation of a Random Forest (RF) algorithm, we achieve a remarkable prediction accuracy of $\mathbf{9 4. 0 7 \%}$ for aggressor nodes, $\mathbf{9 7. 6 \%}$ for victim nodes, and $\mathbf{9 3. 8 5 \%}$ for mitigation schemes.

articleTitle: Network Slice Admission Control for Enhanced Resource Utilization in 6G Multi-UAV Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In the context of 6G networks, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) based edge nodes play a crucial role in delivering accessible, scalable, and low-latency services. Optimizing resource utilization in multi-UAV frameworks require further investigation into user association. Additionally, network slicing allows for the creation of multiple independent, coexisting logical networks, enabling different ground users to share computing, networking, and storage resources. However, due to the finite nature of these resources, service providers cannot meet all user requests. Users often overestimate their resource needs to avoid potential SLA violations. To address these challenges, we introduce a network slice admission control algorithm designed to optimize resource utilization and enhance user association in a UAV environment. We formulated the resource utilization and user association problem as a linear programming problem and solved it using standard optimization tools. To further improve resource utilization and user association, our algorithm employs a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) to dynamically pool resources. Our implementation and evaluation of this algorithm in a 6G-UAV environment demonstrates its superior performance compared to conventional approaches, as confirmed by our numerical analysis.

articleTitle: An SDR Implementation of Frequency Domain Demodulation of LoRaWAN Messages with Temporal Correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper presents a practical LoRaWAN system serving applications that generate time-correlated data, among other applications. For instance, a smart meter reading at a given time can be assumed to be modeled as a random increment from the previous reading. The paper reports a demodulation technique that can be deployed along with existing techniques to detect transmissions from such applications, through a prediction and frequency matching based packet decoding algorithm. We also demonstrate the working of our approach on a software defined radio platform. Practical aspects like energy detection and carrier frequency offsets for LoRa signals are addressed. Limitations of the proposed scheme are provided.

articleTitle: Variational Bayesian Inference-based Robust Channel Estimation for IRS-assisted mmWave MIMO systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) play a significant role in providing enhanced coverage, and improved energy efficiency for millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple input multiple output (MIMO) systems. Performance gains of IRSassisted systems rely heavily on accurate channel state information. Existing works in literature leverage the underlying sparsity of $\mathbf{m m W a v e}$ channels to estimate the cascaded channel between base station (BS), IRS, and user equipment (UE) with low pilot overhead. However, the conventional sparse modelingbased channel estimation approaches yield less accurate channel estimates in practical scenarios where the statistics of the channel and noise are erratic. This work develops novel Variational Bayesian Inference (VBI)-based Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL) algorithms by employing a hierarchical model-based approach capable of capturing the uncertainties in the channel and noise. Simulation results illustrate the superior performance of VBIbased schemes over the conventional SBL channel estimation approaches. Further, the robustness of the proposed schemes for non-ideal and non-Gaussian noise conditions is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Enhanced Angle of Arrival (AoA) Prediction through Neural Networks and Primary and Adjacent Antennas Representation Transformation (PAAR)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this study, we present an enhanced Angle of Arrival (AoA) prediction method using neural networks and the Primary and Adjacent Antennas Representation (PAAR) transformation. PAAR leverages rotational symmetry in segmented antenna data, to transform the data into a rotation-invariant form. Thus, PAAR improves predictive accuracy and stability, especially with limited training data. We conducted experiments with two Digital Video Broadcasting - Terrestrial (DVB-T) datasets and evaluated four different neural network models, each varying in parameter size. Results demonstrate that the PAAR method clearly outperforms the traditional unprocessed approach, which we refer to as the plain approach, in data-limited scenarios, reducing the mean absolute angular error (MAAE) by up to $\mathbf{4 0 \%}$. However, with extensive training data, the plain approach can surpass PAAR due to error propagation. The study demonstrates that the PAAR method effectively enhances AoA prediction, especially with sparse training data.

articleTitle: Effect of Link Margin on Capacity Benefits in Multi-Core Optical Fiber Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Multicore fibers (MCF) promise high capacity benefits to sustain future broadband traffic growth while deploying additional optical equipment like spatial multiplexers and hierarchical optical cross-connects. Therefore network operators will need to exercise usage of additional link margins (LM) as a precaution against equipment degradation that may prevent lightpaths operating at high capacity. However, LM can be reduced by deploying in-line optical performance monitoring (OPM) equipment while incurring additional costs. This paper accounts for the capacity benefits of operating with lower LM while accounting for the cost-per-bit-sec (cpbps) incurred in each LM operation region. Our results indicate that MCF fibers can provide 4.5 times the capacity compared to the traditional single-mode fiber (SMF) network at LM 0 dB while incurring an additional cost of 375 OPMs with a channel launch power of 0 dBm. However, similar capacity benefits can be achieved while reducing channel launch power to -1.5 dBm at LM 2 dB with a lower cost of 309 OPMs. Hence in this paper, we comprehensively correlate the effect of operating with a lower LM, and channel launch power while elaborating upon its trade-offs with cpbps metrics.

articleTitle: Infrastructure Cost Savings with Unbalanced PONs in Rural Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Deployment of Optical Access Networks (OANs) is still a costly process, specially in rural areas, and thus requires detailed and efficient planning. The deployment strategies in rural areas are subjected to challenges posed by demographic and geographical factors. Traditional Balanced Passive Optical Network (BPON) deployments, using symmetrical splitters, which incurs into an inefficient and costly solution due to the sparse user distribution. To address this issue, this paper presents an Hybrid Passive Optical Network (HPON) solution, which combines BPON and Unbalanced Passive Optical Network (UPON) architectures to provide optimal connectivity and reachability. The HPON leverages optical taps in the UPON for fine-grained power distribution. BPON and HPON models are compared in four rural scenarios with varying population densities. The results suggest that the HPON leads to reduced cost per Optical Network Unit (ONU) and cost per unit area compared to BPON, thus providing a solution for the economical deployment of an OAN in rural areas. In the considered rural areas, HPON assures cost savings of up to 25 % over BPON deployments.

articleTitle: Optimizing Synchronization Signal Block Transmissions for Sum-Rate Maximization in Sub-Connected Hybrid Beamforming Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Fifth-generation millimeter wave (mmWave) systems rely on sub-connected (SC) hybrid beamforming architecture due to low power consumption and reduced hardware complexity. These systems require directional beamforming to establish communication between the base station (BS) and user equipment (UE). Typically, the communication between BS and UE occurs in two phases. In the first namely initial access (IA) phase, BS utilizes spatial beam search using synchronization signal (SS) blocks for link establishment and is followed by data transmission in the second phase. As per the 3GPP standard for 5G NR systems, existing approaches utilize a maximum IA duration of 5ms corresponding to the transmission of 64 SS blocks for beam search. The maximum transmission of SS blocks results in a significant delay in data transmission to the user. This work proposes an optimized value of the number of SS block transmissions to achieve a higher sum-rate in an SC hybrid mmWave system. Simulation results demonstrate that an optimized value of SS block transmission results in faster user discovery and yields more time for data transmission. This in turn results in an improved performance of the SC hybrid beamforming systems in terms of enhanced sum-rate capacity and reduced initial beam acquisition time.

articleTitle: A Novel Routing Protocol over Time-Varying IoT Network Using RTS/CTS Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In the context of 6G IoT networks, distributed computing has become a critical enabler for seamless communication across diverse sectors, such as smart manufacturing, intelligent transportation, healthcare, and defense. Many of these applications involve mobile IoT devices (IoDs) that change locations dynamically, requiring robust and efficient multi-hop data transmission frameworks. Selecting the optimal relay node in distributed 6G IoT networks is essential, as it directly impacts energy efficiency, latency, data interference, and throughput. Additionally, ensuring the availability of the relay node’s queue is crucial to prevent data loss. To address these challenges, this work introduces a novel distributed computing framework based on the Request-To-Send (RTS) and Clear-To-Send (CTS) protocols, specifically designed for time-varying 6G IoT networks. The framework incorporates an RTS/CTS mechanism to manage distributed data transfer and employs the Optimal Relay IoD Selection with Q-Learning (OptRISQL) algorithm to determine the optimal relay path dynamically. By distributing computation across nodes, the proposed approach enhances network flexibility, reduces queue sizes, and minimizes memory costs, leading to improved overall network efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that this distributed computing method effectively reduces interference and enhances throughput, outperforming other current state-of-the-art techniques. Index Terms-6G Internet of Things (IoT), Distributed Computing, Request-To-Send (RTS), Clear-To-Send (CTS), Quality-of-Service (QoS).

articleTitle: FUSION: A Flexible Unified Simulator for Intelligent Optical Networking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The increasing demand for flexible and efficient optical networks has led to the development of Software-Defined Elastic Optical Networks (SD-EONs). These networks leverage the programmability of Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and the adaptability of Elastic Optical Networks (EONs) to optimize network performance under dynamic traffic conditions. However, existing simulation tools often fall short in terms of transparency, flexibility, and advanced functionality, limiting their utility in cutting-edge research. In this paper, we present a Flexible Unified Simulator for Intelligent Optical Networking (FUSION), a fully open-source simulator designed to address these limitations and provide a comprehensive platform for SD-EON research. FUSION integrates traditional routing and spectrum assignment algorithms with advanced machine learning and reinforcement learning techniques, including support for the Stable Baselines 3 library. The simulator also offers robust unit testing, a fully functional Graphical User Interface (GUI), and extensive documentation to ensure usability and reliability. Performance evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of FUSION in modeling complex network scenarios, showcasing its potential as a powerful tool for advancing SD-EON research.

articleTitle: TRFI-Net: Modified TRFI-Based Channel Estimation for Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of the Internet of Vehicles, ensuring dependable Vehicle-to-Everything communication is imperative for Intelligent Transportation Systems. The prevailing IEEE 802.11p protocol presents formidable obstacles to accurate channel estimation owing to its standardized pilot patterns. Conventional solutions, such as data pilot-aided methods, are encumbered by error propagation issues stemming from pilot limitations, particularly pronounced at higher speeds. To address these challenges, this paper introduces TRFI-Net, a novel residual network-based channel estimation method with timedomain and frequency-domain interpolation, demonstrating up to a 3 dB gain in high SNR conditions. By harnessing advanced deep learning methodologies and ResNet architecture, TRFI-Net enhances IoV communication resilience. Benchmarking against six channel models and assessing BER and NMSE in the “Roadside unit to vehicle Urban Canyon” scenario highlights TRFI-Net’s efficacy, marking a significant stride in dynamic vehicular channel estimation research.

articleTitle: SmartMME: Implementation of Base Station Switching Off Strategy in ns-3
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In the landscape of next-generation cellular networks, a projected surge of over 12 billion subscriptions foreshadows a considerable upswing in the network’s overall energy consumption. The proliferation of User Equipment (UE) drives this energy demand, urging 5G deployments to seek more energy-efficient methodologies. In this work, we propose SmartMME, as a pivotal solution aimed at optimizing Base Station (BS) energy usage. By harnessing and analyzing critical network states—such as UE connections, data traffic at individual UEs, and other pertinent metrics—our methodology intelligently orchestrates the BS’s power states, making informed decisions on when to activate or deactivate the BS. This meticulous approach significantly curtails the network’s overall energy consumption. In a bid to validate its efficiency, we seamlessly integrated our module into Network Simulator-3 (ns-3), conducting extensive testing to demonstrate its prowess in effectively managing and reducing net energy consumption. As advocates of collaborative progress, we’ve opted to open-source this module, inviting the engagement and feedback of the wider research community on GitHub<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>https://github.com/ns3-dev/ns3-mmwave (Accessed: December 12, 2024)

articleTitle: Node Fault Prediction Assisted Small-World IoT Networks Using ML Frameworks: Towards Performance Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) networks has led to the deployment of large-scale networks, enabling seamless connectivity and data exchange among various devices. To manage the complexity and ensure efficient communication in these expansive networks, adopting suitable network architecture becomes crucial. Small-world networks, characterized by a high Average Clustering Coefficient (ACC) and low Average Path Length (APL), have emerged as a promising architecture for IoT systems due to their efficient communication. However, introducing the Small-World Characteristics (SWC) in an IoT network is challenging due to the need for strategic placement of long-range connections while maintaining low APL and high ACC and ensuring scalability and robustness. In this work, we introduce SWC into the network using an actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm. Additionally, ensuring the reliability of sensor nodes is crucial to maintaining the overall network performance. Therefore, we propose a joint method for dynamic node fault prediction and data routing within small-world IoT networks using advanced Machine Learning (ML) frameworks. Several data routing experiments have been conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach using simulated small-world IoT networks. We analyzed major network parameters such as lifetime, latency, and throughput. We compared the proposed method with existing state-of-the-art approaches and observed promising results.

articleTitle: Non-Uniform Tiling of Point Cloud Layer to Optimize Updates of HD Map Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for the efficient handling of crowd-sourced point cloud data in high-definition (HD) map updates, a critical component for enabling autonomous vehicles. The algorithm employs a non-uniform tiling technique that divides the point cloud layer of the HD map based on detected changes, optimizing data processing while preserving necessary details for accurate map updates. By incorporating caching techniques, the proposed method tackles the limitations and difficulties faced by existing tiling approaches, resulting in improved performance. Specifically, it addresses challenges such as large data volume, transmission overhead, and latency associated with crowd-sourced map updates. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in overcoming these challenges, reducing computation costs, and enhancing the efficiency of HD map updates. Simulation results show that there is 37.5% improvement in caching performance and 27.77% faster data processing in case of non-uniform tiling as compared to uniform tiling scheme.

articleTitle: BioPKI: Identity Authentication with Biometric Public Key Infrastructure in Healthcare Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The constraints of Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), which has been used in critical infrastructure systems since the World Wide Web, remain unresolved. As government-driven digital identification becomes increasingly prevalent around the world particularly in India, it’s critical to understand the shortcomings and threats with PKI particularly in healthcare systems. This paper proposed an approach to enhance the digital identity security process by associating the biometric data with PKI and get around the PKI’s challenges and hazards to be applied in general and in healthcare systems in particular. The proposed approach called BioPKI enhances the security and authentication aspects of digital identity in healthcare setting. This work identified the implementation PKI challenges and proposed the new model termed as BioPKI which associates the biometric information of the user with the public-private key pair generated through RSA algorithm. The Bio-PKI model is tested against various attacks such as key-pair theft, unauthorized access to the pki model, session hijacking, man in the middle attack, and node compromising.

articleTitle: Improving Network Efficiency in Clustered Tree Topology through PSO Optimization in IEEE 802.15.4-DSME based IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The IEEE 802.15.4 standard is designed for low-rate wireless personal area networks (LR-WPANs). Deterministic and Synchronous Multi-channel Extension (DSME) is one of the key Medium Access Control (MAC) modes of the IEEE 802.15.4 standard that was introduced to address the need for higher reliability, lower latency, and better scalability in network communication in Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, in dynamic network conditions (topology and channel traffic), the network suffers from several limitations, such as low packet delivery ratio, high latency and packet collisions, and finally, higher power consumption. This is because of sub-optimal parameter settings. The standard does not define any mechanism to adapt the parameters based on network conditions. In this paper, we propose a mechanism to adapt/fine-tune the network parameters DSME along with the optimization of QoS using an algorithm based on Particle Swarm Optimization(PSO) for dense and dynamic DSME-based IoT networks. Through simulations, the proposed mechanisms’ performance is analyzed in terms of energy efficiency, transmission overhead, throughput, and latency and is shown to outperform the existing DSME MAC scheme.

articleTitle: Inf-TESLA++: A Blockchain-assisted Continuous Authentication Protocol for Broadcast Communication in Resource-Constrained Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Many applications widely use broadcast communications (BC) due to their efficiency in simultaneously distributing data to many receivers. More specifically, BC is essential in resource-constrained devices (RCDs) for conserving energy and bandwidth, which are vital for increasing the longevity and performance of RCDs. The three major challenges in BC are source authentication, data integrity and continuous authentication (CA). The first two challenges are effectively addressed in TESLA and its variants. However, achieving CA without incurring overheads on the sender and receiver sides remains an unresolved challenge. In this paper, we propose Infinite (Inf) TESLA++, assisted by Blockchain and smart contracts, to address the CA challenge with minimal overhead at sender and receiver. Our theoretical and simulation analysis demonstrates that Inf-TESLA++ incurs minimal overhead compared to existing protocols while eliminating the need for direct communication between the sender and receiver for synchronization.

articleTitle: FORCE: Optimal Resource Utilization Framework for Fog-enabled Green Communication in IoMT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has revolutionized healthcare by integrating smart devices to monitor, analyze, and optimize patient care. Various healthcare devices generate a large volume of data daily, which uses a lot of storage and bandwidth. Fog computing is a promising paradigm that extends cloud computing capabilities near the network edge, allowing for real-time processing of healthcare data. In a fog-enabled IoMT environment, effective load balancing is essential to maximize resource utilization and guarantee timely and reliable healthcare services. This paper presents a load-balancing framework, i.e., FORCE, especially for fog-enabled IoMT environments. The FORCE focuses on challenges present in healthcare applications, such as meeting low latency requirements and dynamic workloads, and thus accelerates the idea of faster communication between the end devices, or IoT wearables, and fog nodes. To provide low-latency processing, the framework considers the fog computing architecture and brings computation close to healthcare devices. The FORCE delivers healthcare services with reduced latency and energy consumption. For the scenario wherein the region attribute is used to determine the optimal node result, the time to compute that was obtained is 14.82 seconds. In contrast, the computation time in later scenarios without considering region attributes is $\mathbf{7 6. 8 9}$ seconds. Hence, the FORCE efficiently reduces the searching time for finding the optimal node. Based on the simulation results, it can be concluded that the FORCE effectively optimizes both latency and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Heuristic-based Multicasting Utilizing Network Coding over a Multi-Hop Wireless Mesh Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Multicasting over a multi-hop wireless mesh network is a challenging issue that recently received less attention. Various applications, such as distance learning, telemedicine, web radio, and online conferencing, require the same information to be sent to multiple recipients. In these applications, the destination nodes are often far from the source, necessitating the design of a multi-hop multicasting protocol. This paper proposes an efficient multi-hop multicasting approach for transmitting packets from the source to all intended destinations. By combining network coding with opportunistic routing, the proposed method significantly reduces the expected number of transmissions a packet must undergo in a lossy wireless network. Specifically, this work introduces a Heuristic-Based Multicasting (HBM) scheme that integrates network coding with opportunistic routing. First, it calculates the minimum route cost from the source node to all the destinations. Then, a novel packet transmission strategy is employed, where packets are combined using network coding and transmitted via a path derived from the Network Coding Assisted Multicasting (NCAM) route cost calculation. Extensive simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the NCAM route cost calculation and the corresponding packet transmission strategy. The results show that the proposed HBM scheme significantly reduces the expected number of packet transmissions in the network, thereby increasing throughput compared to existing multicasting schemes such as MORE, Pacifier, and MLCAR.

articleTitle: On Impact of Impulsive Noise on Distributed Heterogeneous Cellular Networks in Industrial IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper evaluates performance of multitier heterogeneous cellular networks (HCNs) with distributed macro-base stations (MBS) and pico-base stations (PBS) using orthogonal multiple access (OMA) to support sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks. In modern industrial environment, an HCN enhances communication by using macro-cells for wide coverage of large machinery and supervisory systems,while pico-cells in densely populated areas like assembly lines provide high data rates and low latency for internet-of-things (IoT) devices, such as sensors and robots. In scenarios such as smart homes, smart grids, and industrial IoT, the deployment is often subject to impulsive electromagnetic interference, significantly affecting the system performance. By employing stochastic geometry, this study investigates and compares the performance change in HCN-OMA under both additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and impulsive noise (Im-N) environments. We employed the Poisson point process (PPP) in HCN to simulate node distributions, as it offers a robust model for evaluating system performance under realistic conditions. The analysis highlights the differences in system behavior across these noise conditions, providing insights into the system’s performance under varying interference scenarios. The evaluation focuses on key performance aspects, such as outage probability, system throughput, and energy efficiency, to analyze the performance of OMA in multi-tier HCNs. The analysis provides insights into the challenges and capabilities of OMA in real-world multi-tier HCN deployments.

articleTitle: Maximizing Profit of the Service Providers through Efficient Content Placement and Retrieval in an IoT-enabled Edge-Cloud Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In today’s 5G era, the amount of data generated by the Internet of Things (IoT) devices is enormous. Data is processed and stored in the cloud under a traditional cloud computing architecture, and real-time processing and retrieval of these data is time-consuming. Therefore, an edge-cloud framework comes in handy where the content generated is placed on the edge nodes of the network, and it can reach the endusers in a time-bound manner. A majority of the previous research works on content placement under the edge-cloud architecture primarily aimed at improving the latency of the system. However, the approach proposed in this paper aims to maximize the profit of the service provider by effectively placing the content in a hierarchically organized edge-cloud network. We propose two strategies and compare them with random and greedy approaches for both synthetic and real data sets. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategies, and the profit of the service providers increases by 38.81% (maximum) and 10.51% (on average) for the synthetic dataset and by 65.74% (maximum) and 22.83% (on average) for the real-world dataset when compared with the greedy approach.

articleTitle: System Level Performance Evaluation of MU-MIMO Precoder Schemes in Advanced Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In 5G and advanced wireless networks, multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) precoding allows multiple users to communicate simultaneously over the same orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) time-frequency resources, thereby increasing the system throughput and improving the user experience. This paper develops and assesses the performance of the inverse discrete Fourier transform (IDFT) based downlink (DL) MU-MIMO precoding techniques at base station (BS) through $3^{\text {rd }}$ generation partnership project (3GPP) defined 5G outdoor channel models using system level simulator (SLS). Further, exploiting the channel reciprocity in case of time division duplex (TDD) deployments, the precoder design discussed in this paper relies on 5G sounding reference signal (SRS) based uplink (UL) channel estimates. Owing to lower complexity of wideband precoder weight computation, this paper presents the performance of wideband IDFT DL precoder and compares it with the maximum theoretical throughput of the network. Moreover, the impact of IDFT precoding techniques on DL key performance indicators (KPI) such as system throughput, precoded DL data signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR), DL scheduled MU-MIMO effective modulation and coding (MCS) are analyzed through SLS. Lastly, the paper compares the proposed SRS based IDFT precoder selection scheme with the existing 3GPP based MU-MIMO precoding schemes relying on channel state information-reference signal (CSI-RS) Type-II codebook.

articleTitle: Assessing Datasets for O-RAN RICs: Hoarding vs Choosing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) is reshaping traditional cellular networks by introducing flexible, interoperable, innovative solutions through open interfaces and RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs). The RICs — Near- and Non-real time (Near-RT and Non-RT) — leverage Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) models for making intelligent decisions, which are critical to enhancing network performance. The effectiveness of the AI/ML models heavily depends on the nature of the training data, with homogeneous and heterogeneous datasets requiring tailored approaches. Existing methods predominantly rely on single statistical measures to determine dataset characteristics, which may not fully capture the complexities of real-world data from the Radio Units (RUs). This paper proposes an Ensemble learning approach that combines multiple statistical distance measures to assess dataset nature robustly, enhancing the accuracy of AI/ML model training. The proposed approach integrates the strengths of various statistical tests such as — Levene’s Test (LT), Bartlett’s Test (BT), Mood’s Median Test (MMT), and Cramér-von Mises Test (CMT). The proposed Ensemble approach achieves superior performance in distinguishing between homogeneous and heterogeneous datasets, leading to more reliable model training by leveraging the complementary properties of the above tests. The results demonstrate that the Ensemble approach outperforms individual measures and shows the most reliable solution for robust dataset identification. The proposed approach not only minimizes the risk of misclassification but also ensures that datasets are accurately identified and processed.

articleTitle: Neural network analysis in detection imperfections of continuous-variable quantum key distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Hacking vulnerabilities in continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) systems are investigated, focusing on practical imperfections in homodyne detection. Specifically, these flaws can be exploited in detector-blinding and detector-saturation attacks, where an eavesdropper can undermine secure communication, especially in CV-QKD. Further, a neural network-based detection method is implemented as a potential countermeasure to classify homodyne detector output voltage data, aiding in identifying such potential hacking scenarios. We obtain an overall accuracy of over $90 \%$ in identifying the attack scenario utilizing a MATLAB neural network model.

articleTitle: Edge-Enabled Downlink Scheduling Scheme for 6TiSCH-Based IIoT Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) with 6G networks promises a huge potential for improvised industrial communication. A large number of low-power communication technologies is expected to be part of 6 G in industrial IoT for data collection, forwarding, and actuation. Industrial IoT (IIOT) requires deterministic network services, which can meet the demand for real-time services. Edge-based solutions can help 6G networks meet the requirements of real-time services demanding lower latency. This work aims to address such real-time demands with efficient use of radio resources using 6TiSCH (IPv6 over Time Slotted Channel Hopping (TSCH) mode). In this paper, we propose an edge-based downlink scheduling scheme for the 6TiSCH-based IIoT network named EDSN. EDSN leverages a computation and communication model using edge computing and 6TiSCH scheduling to minimize the overall network latency for downlink data traffic. It schedules actuation (downlink) signals based on the criticality of the received sensor data and the location of the actuators. EDSN analyzes traffic at the edge nodes and allocates a suitable downlink schedule to meet the application requirements of the edge controller. The scheme offers a fair mechanism for provisioning timely schedules for low-priority packets and significantly reduces downlink action times compared to the state-of-the-art. Our experimental results demonstrate that EDSN can effectively reduce response times and improve packet delivery ratios for priority traffic, making it a promising solution for IIoT applications that require low response times and reliable packet delivery.

articleTitle: Adaptive Unscented Kalman Filter for Time Varying Channel Estimation in OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of channel estimation and symbol detection in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing systems using both the unscented Kalman filter and adaptive unscented Kalman filter techniques. The study investigates the performance of these filters under various modulation schemes, including binary phase shift keying, quadrature phase shift keying, and 16 quadrature amplitude modulation. Using the Rapp model, a simulation study is evaluated for the channel model incorporating non-linear effects, and adaptive filtering parameters are meticulously tuned. Performance metrics such as bit error rate and root mean square error are analyzed as a function of signal-to-noise ratios to compare UKF and AUKF techniques comprehensively. Results indicate that AUKF significantly enhances channel estimation accuracy and reduces BER compared to the traditional UKF, especially under high SNR conditions. The study underscores the potential of adaptive filtering in improving communication reliability in OFDM systems, paving the way for more resilient and efficient wireless communication networks.
